subject: Inference network sandboxing & evidence pack
messages:
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@veridian.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com>
Cc: SOC2 Audits <soc2_audits@veridian.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: network sandboxing / isolation evidence for SIG review

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG and SIG-Lite review for Veridian Health's pilot, the audit team has asked for a short security architecture overview focused on network-level isolation for Redwood's Dedicated and Private offerings. Specifically we need:

- A diagram showing tenant sandboxing across Dedicated pools and Private VPC deployments (subneting, control plane separation, jump hosts).
- A one-page matrix that maps SIG questions related to network isolation/segmentation to where the evidence lives (configs, runbooks, monitoring).
- Notes on egress controls, NAT/bastion patterns, and how KMS/HSM boundaries are enforced during inference.

Target is next Thursday (2027-04-22) for initial artifacts. If you can send what you have sooner that would be great — the SOC2 audit lead may triage additional asks.

Can you also confirm who on your side should be the technical contact for follow-ups?

Appreciate it,
Alex

--
Alex Garcia
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Veridian Health
alex.garcia@veridian.com
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@veridian.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: network sandboxing / isolation evidence for SIG review

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Karthik (security lead, infra) and Laura (customer success lead) — we have an evidence bundle we can share and a short narrative to cover the SIG mappings.

Planned deliverables (by 2027-04-22):
- network_sandbox_diagram_v2.png (attached) — shows Dedicated GPU pools, private-control-plane placement, tenant subneting, and approved egress routes.
- isolation_matrix.csv (attached) — maps SIG/CAIQ items to config/docs/monitoring.
- tenant_fencing_runbook.pdf (attached) — operational steps for isolation incidents and tenant evacuation.
- one-slide executive summary (doc link in Drive).

Technical contact for follow-ups: Karthik Iyer (karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com). He can provide packet-level examples and the runbook owner.

Notes/high level summary (quick):
- Dedicated: logical tenant isolation is enforced at the hypervisor and VPC layer. Tenant workloads run in isolated subnets pinned to reserved GPU pools. Control-plane traffic for Dedicated is handled by a private control plane in a separate management VPC with strict IAM roles and no direct tenant egress.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Customers deploy a control-plane connector; we recommend private peering or transit gateway. Network policies are applied via NF tables on the host and optional cloud firewall rules.
- Egress: Default-deny; allowed egress is explicit and logged. We support per-tenant egress proxies and per-tenant NAT with flow logs forwarded to central monitoring for retention.
- KMS/HSM: Keys for model artifacts and customer data are scoped to tenant projects; HSM-backed keys are used for Private enterprise customers where required.

Attaching the initial artifacts. Let us know if you want a brief walkthrough call — Karthik and I are available tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: (internal) notes for Veridian — mapping + clarifications

Priya / Laura — forwarding internal clarifications I prepared for the SIG mapping we shared. Please include the following bullet points in the matrix and runbook appendix before sending the official bundle to Veridian:

- Subnet mapping: production tenant subnets (10.80.x/24) are isolated per customer pool; control plane subnets are in 10.90.x/24 range and are routed only via peering/VPN to customer management.
- Host-level fences: iptables + eBPF policies enforce process-level egress; we also run an L7 proxy for model artifact retrieval that authenticates via signed tokens.
- KV-cache leakage controls: per-request cache scoping prevents cross-tenant KV reuse; we instrument token correlation and include checks in the audit trail.
- Failover behavior: during Dedicated pool failover we spin tenant VMs in a separate recovery VPC with ephemeral networking; the recovery path has identical firewall and KMS bindings.
- Evidence pointers: VPC flow logs (s3://redwood-audit/vpc-flows/), bastion session records (https://audit.redwood.example.com/sessions), and KMS access logs (HSM audit links included in the CSV).

Attachments included: isolation_matrix.csv, tenant_fencing_runbook.pdf. I also added an appendix column referencing the exact SIG control IDs.

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@veridian.com>

Priya, Karthik —

Received the bundle and skimmed the attachments. This is exactly what the audit team needs for the first pass. Two quick asks: 1) could you provide a one-page signed attestation (PDF) stating that the artifacts are current as of 2027-04-18 and that the control mappings are accurate to the best of your knowledge; and 2) a single-slide summary for our compliance review board that highlights the isolation model, failover protections, and KMS/HSM boundary enforcement.

If you can drop those by EOD tomorrow (04/20) that would keep us on schedule. We may request a short walkthrough call after the board meets.

Thanks again — great turn around.
Alex
